answerText: The claims relate to an extract of the Withania plant. Prior art in TKDL discloses use of Withania somnifera roots for the treatment of stress-related disorders in Ayurveda and Unani systems of medicine. Based on this, the subject matter is not considered novel over the teaching of prior art obtained from TKDL.

citations.actName: CGPDTM Guidelines for Processing of Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material

answerText: Prior art discloses use of German chamomile (from which Chamaemeloside is derived) for wound healing and for treatment of cancer, diabetes, arthritis and eczema in Ayurveda and Unani medicine, though it does not disclose Chamaemeloside itself. The prior art motivates a person skilled in the art to isolate the active ingredient, so isolation and characterization alone does not involve an inventive step.

citations.actName: CGPDTM Guidelines for Processing of Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material

answerText: Independent use of each of these three plants for wound treatment is already disclosed in Ayurveda and Unani medicine. A combination of a plant with known therapeutic effect with further plants of the same known therapeutic effect, all previously known for treating the same condition, is considered an obvious combination.

citations.actName: CGPDTM Guidelines for Processing of Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material

answerText: No prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board is required for local people and communities, cultivators, and vaids, hakims and registered AYUSH practitioners using indigenous medicine — provided that, for cultivated medicinal plants specifically, a certificate of origin is obtained from the Biodiversity Management Committee.

Codified traditional knowledge means the knowledge derived from authoritative books specified in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 — this is the legal test for whether a formulation counts as ‘classical.’
